newsitem.title: USA: NYC comptroller eyes Bd of Ed budget cuts -- paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC comptroller eyes Bd of Ed budget cuts -- paper.

text.p: The New York City Comptroller might order sharp cuts in the Board of Education's budget to stop it from spending state aid that it cannot count on, the New York Post reported Monday.
As a result, the Board of Education has been forced to take out costly, short-term loans, and already has paid $30 million to $40 million in interest.
While New York City is owed nearly $1 billion in back claims for state aid, New York City in its new budget only agreed to pay $35 million of this sum in the first two years.

New York City Comptroller Alan Hevesi told The Post that he will not make a final decision until the state budget was adopted and he has had a chance to study it. "We don't count as revenue allegations of income that aren't real," he was quoted as saying.

School officials have allocated $300 million to upgrade high schools this year. The funds were "rolled over" from expected state aid that never materialized. Hevesi could force the Board of Education to stop rolling over that money, and cough up an extra $100 million or more as a reserve fund.

Deputy Mayor Randy Mastro told the paper there was no need to worry about the potential $400 million shortfall. "It's not going to happen that way for the simple reason that once you have a down payment and commitment to pay the rest, you have concrete action," he told the paper.
